source_text: Sin autem his omnibus in eo, quem suscipiunt a natura, ordine permanentibus adhortationibus, signis, exemplis, promissione vel munerum vel poenarum ad fidem voluntas sine inductione necessitatis allicitur et haec per instituta, per mysteria, per dona non oppressa, sed exspectata, sed libera, sed provocata curatur, apparet, etsi uno spiritu totus mundus vel rugiens vel rabiens refragetur, voluntatem uniuscuiusque, non nativitatem tinctam imitatione fuisse peccati.
pass_a_gloss: But if, with all these remaining in that order which they take up from nature, the will is enticed to faith by exhortations, signs, examples, a promise either of gifts or of punishments without an induction of necessity, and this through ordinances, through mysteries, through gifts not oppressed but expected, but free, but provoked is cured, it appears, even if the whole world roaring or raging resists with one spirit, that the will of each one, not a nativity, was dyed by an imitation of sin.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS exemplum; Blaise Adam as example not transmitter
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice

pass_b_english: But if all these things remain in the order they receive from nature, while the will is attracted to faith by exhortations, signs, examples, and the promise of rewards or punishments, without necessity being imposed; if the will is healed through teachings, mysteries, and gifts—not crushed, but awaited, free, and invited—then it is clear that each person’s will, not birth, was stained by imitation of sin, even if the whole world with one breath roars or rages in opposition.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Adam as example to later sinners, Julian's alternative to tradux.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
